nahhas-meani:1-3.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤـمۤ. غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ فِيۤ أَدْنَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ [verses 1–3].
Mujāhid said: It is al-Jazīra (Upper Mesopotamia), which was the land of the Romans closest to Persia.
Muḥammad ibn Salama al-Aswānī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Sanjar narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Abū Isḥāq al-Fazārī narrated to us, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī ʿAmra, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿الۤـمۤ. غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ﴾: he said: The idolaters liked "Persia" to prevail over "the Romans", because they [the Persians] were idol-worshippers, and the Muslims liked "the Romans" to prevail over "Persia", because they were People of the Book. This was mentioned to Abū Bakr, and Abū Bakr mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Indeed, they will prevail. He said: Abū Bakr mentioned it to them, and they said: Set a term between us and you; if we prevail, we get such-and-such, and if you prevail, you get such-and-such. So he set a term of five years, and they did not prevail. That was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: [Why did you not make it up to less than — I think he said: less than ten?] Saʿīd said: al-biḍʿ is what is less than ten.
Then the Romans prevailed after that, and that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤـمۤ. غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ فِيۤ أَدْنَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ المُؤْمِنونَ بَنَصْرِ اللهِ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: Gambling was lawful at that time. He said: And the Prophet ﷺ said to Abū Bakr: How much is al-biḍʿ? He said: From three to nine.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar read ﴿غَلَبَتِ الرُّومُ﴾ with fatḥa on the ghayn and the lām, and said: they prevailed over the nearest countryside.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning according to the reading of those who read ﴿غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ وَهُم مِّن بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ﴾ is: the Romans, after their defeat — that is, after they were defeated — will prevail.
And whoever reads ﴿سَيُغْلَبونَ﴾, the meaning for him is: and Persia, after their victory — that is, after they had prevailed — will be defeated.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ﴾.
Al-biḍʿ according to Qatāda is more than three and less than ten.
According to al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ: what is less than ten.
According to Abū ʿUbayda: between three and five.
Abū Zayd reported baḍʿ, and it is derived from their saying baḍḍaʿahu when he cut it into pieces; from it comes baḍʿa of meat (a piece of meat), and from it: "he possesses the buḍʿ of the woman", which is only a euphemism for her private part.
In the narration of Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فِي أَدْنَى الأَرْضِ﴾, he said, he says: at the edge of Syria (al-Shām).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied wording (taqdīr) is: in the nearest land to Persia.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِلَّهِ ٱلأَمْرُ مِن قَبْلُ وَمِن بَعْدُ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: When you say ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ and ﴿مِنْ بعدُ﴾, its meaning is: before what you know and after what you know, and before everything and after everything.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is: to Allah belongs the decree of victory, before the victory and after it.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ بِنَصْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is, they will rejoice at Allah's helping the Romans — because they are People of a Book — against Persia, who are Magians; and they will rejoice at the mighty sign which none but Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knows, because He informed them of what would come to pass.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ ظَاهِراً مِّنَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلآخِرَةِ هُمْ غَافِلُونَ﴾.
ʿIkrima and Ibrāhīm said: that is, they know the affairs of their livelihood and the interests of their worldly life.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُواْ فِيۤ أَنفُسِهِمْ مَّا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
That is, except to establish the truth.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَثَارُواْ ٱلأَرْضَ وَعَمَرُوهَآ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا عَمَرُوهَا﴾.
﴿وَأَثَارُواْ ٱلأَرْضَ﴾ means they ploughed it and sowed it, whereas in Mecca there is no ploughing and no sowing.
And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿تُثِيرُ الأَرْضَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ كَانَ عَاقِبَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَاءُواْ ٱلسُّوۤءَىٰ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash read: ﴿ثُمَّ كَانَ عَاقِبَةَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوا السُّوءُ﴾, with السُّوءُ in the nominative.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-sūʾ is the worst of evil, and al-sūʾā is the fuʿlā form of it.
It has also been said: ﴿ٱلسُّوۤءَىٰ﴾ here is the Fire, just as al-ḥusnā is Paradise.
The meaning of ﴿أَسَاءُوا﴾ here is: they associated partners [with Allah]; this is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أَن كَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Al-Kisāʾī said: that is, because they denied the signs of Allah.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ يُبْلِسُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: they will be dejected.
Abū Yaḥyā related from Mujāhid, who said: al-iblās is disgrace.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said أَبْلَسَ الرجلُ when a man is bewildered and grieved, and his argument fails him so that he cannot find his way to it, and he despairs of good, as [the poet] said:
* "قَالَ نَعَمْ أَعرِفُه وَأَبْلَسَا" *
(He said: Yes, I know it — and fell dumbfounded.)

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ فَهُمْ فِي رَوْضَةٍ يُحْبَرُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿يُحْبَرونَ﴾ means they are made to enjoy bliss.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its literal sense is that the traces of blessing become visible on them.
From that comes al-ḥabr, and "on his teeth is a ḥabra (a stain)".
Al-Awzāʿī related from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr: ﴿فِي رَوْضَةٍ يُحْبَرُونَ﴾, he said: listening [to song] in Paradise.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ ٱللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The five prayers are in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; and he recited the verse: ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ ٱللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ﴾, he said: Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ; ﴿وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ﴾, he said: Fajr; ﴿وَعَشِيَّاً﴾: ʿAṣr; ﴿وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُون﴾: Ẓuhr.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُخْرِجُ ٱلْحَيَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَيِّتِ وَيُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَيِّتَ مِنَ ٱلْحَيِّ وَيُحْيِي ٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَكَذَلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ﴾.
There are several views on its meaning:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: that is, He brings the sperm-drop out of the man, and the man out of the sperm-drop.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: And likewise the egg.
Salmān said: He brings the believer out of the unbeliever and the unbeliever out of the believer; and al-Ḥasan said the same.
It has also been said: He causes the living to die and gives life to the dead.
﴿وَيُحْيِي ٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَكَذَلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ﴾,
that is, just as He gives life to the earth with plants.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن تُرَابٍ﴾.
The meaning is: that He created your origin, who is "Adam", peace be upon him, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ الْقَرَْيَةَ﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. with the muḍāf omitted].
It is also possible that the [seminal] fluid is created from dust.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجاً لِّتَسْكُنُوۤاْ إِلَيْهَا﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: that Eve was created from Adam.
The other: that the meaning is: He created for you mates of your own kind, because a human being is more at ease with his own kind and finds more repose in it. Similar to it is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسِ وَاحِدَةٍ وَجَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا لِيَسْكُنَ إلَيْهَا﴾.
Both views apply to its meaning.
That is, He made from its kind its mate; and this points to both sexes together. The pronoun in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿جَعَلاَ لَهُ شُرَكَاءَ فِيمَا آتَاهُمَا﴾ would then refer to the two sexes, and the pronoun in His saying ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ refers to the two sexes because they are a multitude.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُم مَّوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: affection (al-mawadda) is intercourse, and mercy (al-raḥma) is the child.
It has also been said: affection and mercy are the inclining of their hearts towards one another.
And the meaning is: and among His signs that point to His oneness, and that He has no partner and no equal.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
﴿ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ means for the jinn and mankind.
And ﴿ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ has also been reported, and it is good.
[Translator's note: the second word is printed with the same vowelling as the first; the reported variant is evidently لِلْعالِمِين ("for those who know"), with kasra on the lām.]

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ ٱلْبَرْقَ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً﴾.
The meaning is: and He shows you the lightning, [which is] among His signs; one clause is conjoined to another.
It is also possible that the meaning is: and among His signs is a sign by which He shows you the lightning, as the poet said:
وَمَا الدَّهْرُ إلاَّ تَارَتَانِ فمنهما * أَمُوتُ وأُخْرَى أَبْتَغِي العَيْشَ أَكْدَحُ
(Time is nothing but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek a living, toiling.)
[Translator's note: the verse is cited for an omitted noun after «فمنهما», i.e. "of them is [a time in which] I die".]
The fear is for the traveller, and the hope is for the one at home.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَن تَقُومَ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلأَرْضُ بِأَمْرِهِ﴾.
That is, that the two of them remain standing.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَهُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ كُلٌّ لَّهُ قَانِتُونَ﴾.
This too is among His signs, and [the words "among His signs"] were omitted because there is an indication of them in the context.
Al-qānit is the one who stands in obedience.
And the standing here is submission to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, whether the servants like it or dislike it.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَبْدَأُ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
There are three views on its meaning:
a- In the narration of Ṣāliḥ from Ibn Anas: ﴿وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيهِ﴾ means it is easier for the created being, because He began its creation from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, whereas the restoration is by His saying to it ﴿كَنْ فَيكُونُ﴾; and that is easier for the created being.
[Translator's note: «ابن انس» is as written in the source; this explanation is usually reported via Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās.]
b- Mujāhid said: The restoration is easier for Him than the beginning, and all of it is easy for Him.
The meaning on this view is: it is easier for Him in your estimation and in terms of what you know, by way of comparison; and after it comes ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلْمَثَلُ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ﴾.
c- Qatāda said: ﴿وَهُوَ أَهْوْنُ عَلَيْهِ﴾ means it is easy. This is a good view; from it is "Allāhu akbar", meaning great (kabīr), and from it is the poet's saying:
لَعَمْرُكَ مَا أَدْرِي وَإنَّي لأَوْجَلُ * عَلَى أَيِّنَا تَعْدُو المَنِيَّةُ أَوَّلُ
(By your life, I do not know — and I am indeed afraid — upon which of us death will fall first.)
And the saying of the other:
إنَّ الَّذِي سَمَك السَّماءَ بنى لَنَا * بَيْتَاً دَعَائِمُهُ أعزُّ وأَطْوَلُ
(He who raised up the sky built for us a house whose pillars are mighty and tall.)
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿وهو هيِّنٌ عليه﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلْمَثَلُ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He is saying ﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ﴾.
It has also been said: it means "there is no god but Allah".
Its literal sense in the language is: and to Him belongs the highest description.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ضَرَبَ لَكُمْ مَّثَلاً مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: This is a parable that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, struck for the idolaters, saying: ﴿هَلْ لَّكُمْ مِّن مَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ مِّن شُرَكَآءَ فِي مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ فَأَنتُمْ فِيهِ سَوَآءٌ﴾, that is, would any of you be content for his slave to be like him in his wealth and his person? If you are not content with this, how then have you assigned a partner to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He?
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view; that is, would any of you be content to make his slave like himself — that is, like his free partner, without whom he settles no matter? As He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَلْمِزُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾, that is, let none of you find fault with another.
So too His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿كَخِيفَتِكُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ﴾; and as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَوْلاَ إذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ المُؤْمِنُونَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتُ بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ خَيْرَاً﴾; and as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾.
It has also been said: as its spending is feared from your side.
That is, you do not make your slaves like yourselves, while all of you are slaves of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; how then do you assign to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, a partner, when there is nothing like Him?

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفاً فِطْرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا﴾.
Al-fiṭra is the beginning of creation; from it comes ﴿فَاطِرُ السَّمَواتِ﴾, and from it "the camel's canine tooth faṭara (broke through)", and from it "faṭartu the well", that is, I began digging it.
That is, He began their creation on the basis that they know they have a Creator and a Disposer.
In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Every child is born upon the fiṭra, until his parents are the ones who make him a Jew or make him a Christian."
Al-Awzāʿī and Ḥammād ibn Salama said: This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَإذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَتَهُمْ﴾.
The meaning on this view is: every child is born upon the covenant that was taken from him.
And in the ḥadīth: "He brought them out like tiny ants and took the covenant from them." So every child is born upon that covenant — even if he ascribes his worship to other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, or describes Him with other than His attribute — until his parents teach him Judaism and Christianity.
It has also been said: upon the natural constitution that you know, distinguishing nothing.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak said: This is for whoever will be a Muslim;
he holds that it is specific.
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This was before the obligations were revealed and jihad was commanded.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting of them is the first view; it is the view of the people of the Sunna, and it agrees with the language.
It cannot be abrogated, because it is a report, nor can it be specific. The meaning of the ḥadīth only became problematic because they interpreted "al-fiṭra" as Islam, whereas it is only the beginning of creation.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَلاَ تَكُونُواْ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾.
﴿مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ﴾ means returning to Him in obedience.
And the meaning is: so set your faces, turning [to Him] (munībīna).
[Translator's note: i.e. ﴿مُنِيبِينَ﴾ is ḥāl (circumstantial) to the plural subject understood in ﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ﴾ of verse 30.]
And the meaning of ﴿كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾
is: each says, "I am upon guidance."

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلنَّاسَ ضُرٌّ دَعَوْاْ رَبَّهُمْ مُّنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
That is, they sought refuge with none but Him, and abandoned what they used to worship besides Him.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَكْفُرُواْ بِمَآ آتَيْنَاهُمْ فَتَمَتَّعُواْ فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
So He moved from the report [in the third person] to direct address; and this is by way of threat and warning, as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُلِ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَمَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِنْ وَمَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَاناً فَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِمَا كَانُواْ بِهِ يُشْرِكُونَ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Every sulṭān in the Qurʾan is an excuse and a proof."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is: or have We sent down to them a book in which there is an excuse, or a proof, or evidence, that directs them to associating partners?

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَآ أَذَقْنَا ٱلنَّاسَ رَحْمَةً فَرِحُواْ بِهَا﴾.
That is, a blessing, they rejoice in it.
﴿وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ﴾, that is, and if a misfortune befalls them.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَآتِ ذَا ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ حَقَّهُ وَٱلْمِسْكِينَ وَٱبْنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
Qatāda said: If you do not give to your kinsman and walk to him on your own feet, you have cut him off.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ آتَيْتُمْ مِّن رِّباً لِّيَرْبُوَ فِي أَمْوَالِ ٱلنَّاسِ فَلاَ يَرْبُو عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid and Ibn ʿAbbās said: It is the man who gives a gift to another man and seeks something better than it in return; he has no reward for it, and no sin upon him.
ʿIkrima said: Ribā is of two kinds: a lawful ribā and an unlawful ribā. As for the lawful, it is that a man gives another something so that he will give him more than it; this does not increase with Allah. The unlawful is in deferment (al-nasīʾa).
Ibrāhīm said: This was in the Jāhiliyya: a man would give his kinsman wealth so that it would multiply with him; it does not increase with Allah.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ آتَيْتُمْ مِّن زَكَاةٍ تُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُضْعِفُونَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿مِّن زَكَاةٍ﴾ means of charity.
Then He said ﴿فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُضْعِفُونَ﴾, that is, those who find manifold of that, that is, possessors of multiplication, as you say: rajulun muqwin, that is, a man possessing strength.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ظَهَرَ ٱلْفَسَادُ فِي ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي ٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فِي ٱلْبَرِّ﴾: the son of Adam's killing of his brother; ﴿وَٱلْبَحْرِ﴾: the seizing of the ship by force.
ʿIkrima and Qatāda said: the land is the deserts, and the sea is the towns.
Qatāda said: And the corruption is shirk (associating partners).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied wording on this view is: and in the places of the sea, that is, those lying on the sea.
The best that has been said about this verse — and Allah knows best — is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās. Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ظَهَرَ ٱلْفَسَادُ فِي ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ﴾:
he says: the diminishing of blessing because of the deeds of the servants, so that they may repent.
The meaning on this view is: drought has appeared on land and sea because of people's sins.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينَ ٱلْقِيِّمِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لاَّ مَرَدَّ لَهُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ﴾.
That is, direct your aim to the upright religion before the Day of Resurrection comes, when no soul's faith will benefit it if it had not believed before.
The meaning of ﴿يَصَّدَّعُونَ﴾ is: they will be divided, a party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحاً فَلأَنفُسِهِمْ يَمْهَدُونَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿فَلأَنفُسِهِمْ يَمْهَدُونَ﴾: in the grave.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of ﴿يَمْهَدُونَ﴾ in the language is: they smooth [a place] for themselves by good works; from al-mihād, which is the bed.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُهُ كِسَفاً فَتَرَى ٱلْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلاَلِهِ﴾.
﴿وَيَجْعَلُهُ كِسَفاً﴾: [kisaf is] the plural of kisfa, which is a piece.
﴿فَتَرَى ٱلْوَدْقَ﴾: Mujāhid said: that is, the rain. ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلاَلِهِ﴾, that is, from between the clouds.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن قَبْلِهِ لَمُبْلِسِينَ﴾.
On the repetition of ﴿قَبْلِ﴾ here there are three views:
a- Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: This is by way of tawkīd (emphasis), and most of the grammarians hold this view.
b- Quṭrub said: that is, though they were, before the sending down, before the rain…
c- The third view is, in my opinion, the best of them: that the meaning is "before the clouds", that is, before seeing the clouds, they were despairing; and the clouds have been mentioned before.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰ آثَارِ رَحْمَتِ ٱللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُحْيِيِ ٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَآ﴾.
﴿رَحْمَتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: that is, the rain is of Allah's mercy. ﴿كَيْفَ يُحْيِيِ ٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَآ﴾.
Muḥammad al-Yamānī read: ﴿كَيْفَ تُحْيى الأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا﴾.
The meaning according to his reading is: how the mercy gives life to the earth, or the traces [do so].
And ﴿يُحْيِي﴾ with yāʾ means: Allah gives life, or the rain, or the trace — for whoever reads it thus.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنَا رِيحاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرّاً لَّظَلُّواْ مِن بَعْدِهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾.
The grammarians said: ﴿فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرّاً﴾ means they saw the vegetation yellowed; its literal sense is: they saw the trace yellowed. ﴿لَّظَلُّواْ مِن بَعْدِهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ means layaẓallunna (they would surely remain); this is the view of al-Khalīl.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This occurs with the particles of condition (ḥurūf al-mujāzāt).

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنَّكَ لاَ تُسْمِعُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَلاَ تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا وَلَّوْاْ مُدْبِرِينَ﴾.
That is, they are in the position of the dead and the deaf, because they do not accept, owing to their obstinacy.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن تُسْمِعُ إِلاَّ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِآيَاتِنَا فَهُمْ مُّسْلِمُونَ﴾.
That is, you make none hear except one who is receptive, not obstinate.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن ضَعْفٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةٍ﴾.
﴿خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن ضَعْفٍ﴾ means from semen.
﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةٍ﴾ means youth.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ يُقْسِمُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ مَا لَبِثُواْ غَيْرَ سَاعَةٍ﴾.
That is, they swear that they remained in the graves no more than a single hour.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ كَانُواْ يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾.
That is, thus they used to lie in this world.
It is said أُفِكَ الرَّجُل when a man is turned away from truth and good; and arḍun maʾfūka is land withheld from rain.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْعِلْمَ وَٱلإِيمَانَ لَقَدْ لَبِثْتُمْ فِي كِتَابِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْبَعْثِ﴾.
It has been said: the meaning is: according to the report of the Book of Allah, you remained in your graves until the Day of Resurrection.
It has also been said: there is a fronting and deferring (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in the wording,
and the meaning is: and those who were given knowledge in the Book of Allah said: you have remained until the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱصْبِرْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلاَ يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُوقِنُونَ﴾.
﴿وَلاَ يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ﴾ means let them not provoke you; ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ means those who doubt.
